newsitem.title: USA: American attempts around-the-world balloon flight.
newsitem.headline: American attempts around-the-world balloon flight.

text.p: The third attempt in less than a week to make an around-the-world balloon flight was in its final countdown on Monday, an expedition official said.
Steve Fossett, 52, a wealthy Colorado-based commodities broker, planned to lift off from Busch Stadium in downtown St. Louis late on Monday night or early on Tuesday.
"We believe it's going to go. The jet stream looks good right now," expedition spokesman Bo Kemper said.

The attempt follows recent failures by rival teams in Europe and North Africa to crack one of manned flight's great barriers -- a goal that also eluded Fossett a year ago when his balloon crashed in Canada during a similar attempt.

On Sunday a balloon piloted by Bertrand Piccard and Wim Verstraeten ditched in the Mediterranean six hours after taking off from the Swiss Alps. Fumes from kerosene leaking into the cabin brought down the Swiss team.

Last Wednesday British tycoon Richard Branson and two crew members brought their Virgin Global Challenger balloon down in Algeria less than 24 hours after taking off from Morocco. The craft had suddenly lost lift and plunged.

Unlike the other recent expeditions, American Fossett would be flying alone. He already holds a world distance record for a solo balloon flight set in 1995 when he flew from South Korea to Canada. His "Solo Spirit" craft gets its lift from helium and hot air, as did the Swiss and British craft.
Jet streams dipping farther south at high speeds during the Northern Hemisphere winter make January a favoured time for such long-distance balloon flights.
